briefing.opening: Good morning, everyone. I will now begin the daily climate change briefing for August 7, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Climate Disasters: Global Heatwaves and Wildfire Proliferation
sections.content: According to reports today, extreme heatwaves and large-scale wildfires are leading to climate disasters worldwide. Domestically, despite the traditional start of autumn (Ipchu), heatwave advisories have been issued across most parts of the country, with peak sensible temperatures approaching 39 degrees Celsius. A severe heatwave warning has been issued for all of Seoul, and temperatures exceeding 35 degrees Celsius are forecast to continue until next week [46, 48, 51]. Notably, 20% of heat-related illness patients are occurring at home, with the elderly being particularly vulnerable, highlighting the urgent need for improved residential environments [52, 54]. Internationally, large-scale wildfires in Canada have led to a fivefold increase in extreme wildfire risk, with reports indicating nearly double the likelihood of wildfires in Ontario and the Northwest Territories [55, 62, 64, 65, 69, 73, 75, 78, 81, 83, 84, 86, 87, 88, 89]. In the UK, extreme heatwaves are also leading to growing warnings of excess mortality, infrastructure problems, and potential food shortages [95].

sections.title: ⚠️ Rapid Ecosystem Changes and the Reality of the Climate Crisis
sections.content: Climate change is causing widespread and rapid changes in ecosystems. In Kenya, lake overflows and crocodile sightings have occurred [1]. In Cape Cod, USA, changes have been observed, making it a habitat for tiger sharks [61]. According to domestic and international research, global butterfly habitats are rapidly being reshaped [2, 59, 85, 91]. In the Western United States, severe snow droughts are becoming more frequent [71]. Furthermore, a green algae warning has been issued in the Nakdong River estuary, and threats to aquatic ecosystems are materializing, such as the bottom of Okjeong Lake in Imsil-gun, Jeollabuk-do, being exposed due to heatwaves and drought [53]. There are also warnings that these climate changes could lead to 'climateflation,' potentially impacting our dinner tables [17].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Domestic Climate Response Policies and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Domestic policy discussions and adaptation efforts to address the climate crisis are actively underway. Haenam County Mayor Myung Hyun-gwan emphasized the urgency of establishing and operating the National Agri-Food Climate Change Response Center and requested national funding [3, 10, 11]. The necessity of a 'climate audit' to reduce climate change damages, such as heatwaves, has also been raised [4, 5]. President Lee Jae-myung defined heatwaves as a 'national climate disaster' and called for comprehensive responses and infrastructure improvements [19]. Local governments are actively engaged in various practical activities to adapt to climate change, including operating mobile shelters during heatwaves [21], energy saving and carbon neutrality campaigns [22], expanding carbon neutrality education at corporate sites [23], creating carbon-neutral gardens [24, 27], and operating mobile carbon neutrality point registration desks [25, 29]. Jeju Island and Sangju City, among others, are making efforts to enhance cultivation stability by supplying and diversifying crop varieties adapted to climate change [6, 8].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Increasing Industry's Role
sections.content: Domestically and internationally, interest and investment in renewable energy transition are expanding. HD Hyundai Construction Equipment is accelerating its renewable energy transition to achieve RE100, doubling the use of renewable energy at its Incheon plant [31, 39]. Tax credit support for domestic production in key sectors such as renewable energy, batteries, and semiconductors is planned [32]. Shinhyup is expanding regional renewable energy investments, including deciding on 100 billion won in financial support for the Jeonbuk offshore wind power project [33, 36, 43]. In Haenam, Jeollanam-do, construction has begun on the nation's largest 400 MW solar power complex [35]. Efforts to gather on-site opinions and institutionalize the spread of agrivoltaics are also continuing [38, 42]. A plan to use wind power generation profits for cooling costs for heatwave-vulnerable households is also being pursued [41]. These efforts are leading to strong performance of renewable energy-related stocks in the domestic stock market, garnering positive market reactions [37, 45].

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Change Perception and Policy Debates
sections.content: In the international community, various discussions are unfolding regarding the perception of climate change and response measures. Regarding the cause of the Canadian wildfires, scientists point to climate change, while former U.S. President Donald Trump blames mismanagement, leading to ongoing debate [55, 64, 69, 73, 75, 78, 83]. Criticism has also been raised that major media outlets omitted mentions of climate change in their reporting on U.S. heatwaves, suggesting the need for reflection on how climate change is covered [72]. Meanwhile, China has announced a new five-year climate change plan, demonstrating its commitment to climate action [56, 96]. Changes are also being observed in the agricultural sector, with Tasmanian cherry farmers facing climate change making adaptation efforts [79].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of climate disasters and the multifaceted response efforts both domestically and internationally. Only sustained attention and action can safeguard humanity's future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
